questions.question: In S-cam brakes, rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. When does this air pressure enter?

options.text: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
When the driver uses the emergency brake.
When the driver uses the trailer hand valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the driver presses the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Pressing the brake pedal sends air into the brake chambers. This air pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters. The slack adjusters then twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: If you cannot tell if the road is icy and slippery, what should you do?

options.text: Guess whether the road is icy.
Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.
Look at the road closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely icing over too.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved mirrors found on many large vehicles. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, how should you identify the hazardous materials?

options.text: Smell the materials.
Touch the materials.
Check the shipping papers.

questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Never touch or smell leaking hazardous materials. Doing so could cause serious injury or death.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you should not worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.
The valve is working correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air to prevent the system pressure from getting too high. If it starts releasing air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic inspect and fix the problem.

questions.question: What should you know about the radiator cap?

options.text: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
You can remove it when the coolant is hot.
It should be cool to the touch during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap while the cooling system is hot. Opening it could release steam and boiling water that could severely burn you. If the cap is cool to the touch, the system is likely cool enough to open.

questions.question: What happens after two violations of state hand-held mobile phone use laws?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
Your CDL will be disqualified.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted twice of violating state hand-held mobile phone use laws, your CDL will be disqualified. Penalties increase with more violations.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, why is turning toward the driver's side recommended?

options.text: The driver has the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has the best view.
questions.explanation: When backing, turn the vehicle toward the left (driver's) side. This gives the driver the best possible view of the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows wheels to lock up.
It prevents wheels from locking up.
It makes the vehicle easier to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking during hard braking. When ABS detects that wheels are about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking out a window.
Inside the vehicle, awake or asleep.
Within 100 feet of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?

options.text: Stay fit and healthy
Keep the cab warm
Eat heavy foods

questions.explanation: Heavy foods and warm cabs make you sleepy. Exercise and a healthy diet help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not require spring brakes. Use wheel chocks when parking these trailers to keep them from rolling.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, what should you check?

options.text: Check the hoses for leaks.
Make sure hoses are connected to the battery.
Check that hoses carry fuel.

questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels for leaks.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle.
Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to get off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Find emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing and call 911.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure you are rested.
Make sure your glasses are clean.
Wear sunglasses.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses at night. Keep your eyeglasses clean and unscratched. Get rest before driving at night.

questions.question: What is it to carry gases or liquids in a leaking tank?

options.text: Discouraged.
Acceptable on short trips.
Illegal.

questions.explanation: Check the tank for dents or cracks before driving. Look under the vehicle for leaks. It is illegal to carry gases or liquids in a leaking tank.

questions.question: What should you do when driving a large truck to not slow traffic?

options.text: Switch gears while driving uphill.
Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you NOT check?

options.text: Too much air pressure in your tires.
Too little air pressure in your tires.
That all tires are the same brand.

questions.correctAnswerText: That all tires are the same brand.
questions.explanation: Check that your tire pressure is not too high or too low. The tire brand does not matter.

questions.question: What is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces called?

options.text: White ice.
Black ice.
Blue ice.

questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like wet pavement. Be careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.
